trust_decision.summary: Whether a link href carried in untrusted document data (JSON drop payload, or text attributes the HTMLParser takes from data-trix-attributes) is a safe URL; the fix decides it at model deserialization (StringPiece.fromJSON) with DOMPurify.isValidAttribute, because the render sink never checks it.

landing_point.why: The summary names HTMLParser attribute injection on paste; getTextAttributes merges the JSON in data-trix-attributes (kept by the sanitizer hook, src/trix/models/html_sanitizer.js:13-16) straight into text attributes, which is where a reader starts.

fix_sites.entry_point: Document.fromJSON / Document.fromJSONString, reached by drop of application/x-trix-document (src/trix/controllers/level_0_input_controller.js:124-138), Editor.loadJSON (src/trix/models/editor.js:27-28), deserializeFromContentType (src/trix/core/serialization.js:77-79) and every HTMLParser.getDocument (src/trix/models/html_parser.js:80)
same API, via the prebuilt bundle shipped in the action_text-trix Ruby gem
fix_sites.module_kind: generated bundle copy (second packaging of the same code)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/trix/models/string_piece.js:6-8 (JSON deserializer, not the HTMLParser named by the report); also the bundled copy action_text-trix/app/assets/javascripts/trix.js:6865

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about HTML paste, and HTMLSanitizer already strips javascript: hrefs (src/trix/models/html_sanitizer.js:91-95), so the JSON deserializer and the drop/loadJSON path look like a separate internal format; insertLink and activateAttribute look like trusted user/developer input.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Safe links (https, relative, mailto) must survive deserialization with their text; data-trix-attributes must still carry legit attachment attributes (caption, presentation); an over-broad fix that drops data-trix-attributes or all hrefs breaks round-trip copy/paste and drag of links and captions.

O7_producer.where: src/trix/models/html_parser.js:41-47 and :323-329 (parseTrixDataAttribute JSON → piece attributes), consumed by src/trix/models/string_piece.js:6-8

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Level 2 beforeinput insertLink sets href from event.data with no URL validation, inserting a StringPiece directly (no fromJSON)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Browser-originated user action on the user's own editor; looks like self-XSS, and the toolbar route has its own check (src/trix/controllers/toolbar_controller.js:224-230)
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: controllers package, 2 files from string_piece.js (via src/trix/models/composition.js:354-366)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Public Editor.activateAttribute('href', value) → Composition.setTextAttribute builds a StringPiece via Text.textForStringWithAttributes, bypassing the fromJSON check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Developer API, so the caller is trusted; the published fix only covered untrusted deserialized data

O8b_injection_room.sibling: AttachmentPiece.fromJSON passes pieceJSON.attributes through; a planted attachment-level link attribute rendered without the attachment_view check would mirror the bug
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The href check for attachments lives only in the view (src/trix/views/attachment_view.js:128-135), so a maintainer adding a new link-like attribute could easily skip it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Block.fromJSON takes htmlAttributes from JSON; a config-allowlisted URL-valued block htmlAttribute (e.g. cite) would be rendered unchecked by src/trix/views/block_view.js:60-63
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The htmlAttributes allowlist checks names only, never values, so a URL-type addition is a plausible feature

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second groupTagName text attribute (or custom textAttributes config) whose value lands in an element attribute at render time without validation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The render sink trusts model attributes; config.textAttributes is app-extensible

O9_family: CWE-79 stored/DOM XSS via javascript: URL in a deserialized link attribute

O10_build.toolchain: Node >= 18, yarn, rollup, @web/test-runner with Playwright/WebDriver browsers, QUnit

j_defence_ineffective=1 rests on HTMLSanitizer's href protocol check (src/trix/models/html_sanitizer.js:91-95) never seeing hrefs carried inside data-trix-attributes JSON, which the hook keeps (src/trix/models/html_sanitizer.js:13-16).

Pattern A is weak: there is only one real source site (plus a generated bundle copy); its strength is the layer gap between the HTMLParser report and the deserializer fix. The Pattern B routes are user- or developer-originated, so they are realistic only as reason-to-dismiss levers.
